title: Native Flavors Take Center Stage in Albuquerque
summary:
Just a couple of miles off Route 66 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, there is a restaurant where Native American dishes take center stage.

Indian Pueblo Kitchen sits beside the Indian Pueblo Cultural Center, a museum and cultural center founded in 1976 by the 19 Pueblo tribes of New Mexico.

One regular, Rolf Pendall, started with blue corn waffles for breakfast dessert, then helped finish his sweetheart's plate of enchiladas and pinto beans.

The menu is all Native American and Southwestern-inspired. Diners can order blue corn enchiladas “Christmas style,” with one side covered in red chile sauce and the other in green. There is chile posole with beef short ribs served on the bone, and Indian tacos on homemade fry bread. One dish is a social media favorite: pickles marinated in cherry Kool-Aid, deep-fried, and served with green chile ranch sauce.

The star baker is Rita Toledo, from Jemez Pueblo. Her specialty is biscochitos, fragrant shortbread cookies spiced with anise and rolled in cinnamon sugar. Biscochitos are New Mexico's state cookie. Toledo has added her own twists, including a chile pepper version with a little kick at the end.

Her biscochitos are so popular that the restaurant sells them at its café inside Albuquerque's airport, and she makes at least 48 dozen each week just for that location.

Kathy Allio and Jeff Allen, visiting from Pennsylvania, tried a bowl of bean chili with elk meat. Allio said the red chiles were flavorful without being hot.

Fragua said the center sits on land where the Albuquerque Indian School once operated, a boarding school that ran from 1881 to the early 1980s. She said the campus is now built on resilience, empowering Pueblo voices and telling the stories of who Native people are.
why_it_matters: Food is one way communities keep their culture alive and share it with others, and this restaurant shows how Pueblo traditions, from blue corn to biscochitos, are still being cooked, enjoyed, and passed on today.

background_read: Pueblo peoples are Native American communities in New Mexico, each with its own village, traditions, and food.
Their cooking uses local ingredients such as blue corn, beans, and chile peppers, and dishes like enchiladas, posole, and fry bread are shared at family meals and celebrations.
The Indian Pueblo Cultural Center was founded by the 19 Pueblo tribes of New Mexico to share their history and culture, and its restaurant serves the foods of those communities.
The center stands on land where the Albuquerque Indian School once operated, a boarding school that ran from 1881 to the early 1980s, and today the campus focuses on Pueblo voices and stories.
